title: Richards Embedded Mass-Conservative Temporal Estimator Feasibility and Reference Construction
purpose: Assess and reconstruct the smallest Richards-owner temporal error estimator/reference route that can be independently qualified without relying on an unavailable over-refined backward-Euler endpoint and without weakening hard mass conservation.

candidate_routes.name: embedded_mass_conservative_temporal_estimator
required_properties: pressure-head temporal error estimate is explicit and dimensional
principal state advance remains mass-conservative in water content/storage
estimator is model-owned rather than F-GC-specific
error estimate does not require an unavailable N1024/N2048 backward-Euler endpoint
attempt can be computed transactionally from committed state
bounded additional solve cost can be stated before production admission

candidate_routes.name: residual_based_a_posteriori_richards_estimator
required_properties: time-discretization and linearization contributions are separable
norm and reliability statement are transferable or explicitly rederived for the SWAP discretization

candidate_routes.name: method_of_manufactured_solutions
required_properties: manufactured source and boundary terms are explicit
mass accounting is checked against the manufactured source
MMS is not used by itself to claim production-physics estimator validity

pre_rejected_shortcuts: increase production or qualification max_iterations solely to manufacture a deeper backward-Euler reference
increase max_backtracking solely to manufacture a deeper backward-Euler reference
relax nonlinear head tolerance to manufacture a reference
widen the F-VQ29 machine-floor rule after observing failure
relabel N512 as exact or sufficient reference contrary to F-VQ29
reuse F-VQ28 transaction retry shortening as equivalent to same-horizon refinement
use mass closure as a proxy for temporal accuracy
gate_A_questions: What exact temporal approximation and embedded error formula does candidate A require?
Can candidate A be expressed over the existing SWAP semi-discrete mixed Richards state without changing physical equations?
What additional history/scratch is required, and can it remain worker-local or attempt-local?
Does candidate A preserve exact ledger mass conservation independently of its error estimator?
Can candidate A provide an estimator from a bounded number of solves per attempted interval?
Which statements from candidate B are mathematically transferable to SWAP and which require rederivation?
Which MMS case can independently verify temporal order, estimator response and mass accounting before any physical-envelope qualification?

exit_gates.A_feasible: A source- and literature-bound embedded estimator contract is reconstructed, its state/scratch/cost semantics fit SWAP invariants, and a test-only prototype plan can be frozen without choosing a scientific tolerance.
exit_gates.A_not_feasible: The literature method depends on state variables, discretization properties or nonlinear solves that cannot be mapped without changing SWAP physics or violating bounded-cost/mass requirements.
exit_gates.independent_followup_required: Any implemented estimator must pass a later F-VQ held-out qualification before runtime acceptance can consume it.
